newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels Bel-20 enters Easter break on firm note.
newsitem.headline: Brussels Bel-20 enters Easter break on firm note.

text.p: The Bel-20 index gained one percent on Thursday on window-dressing ahead of a four-day Easter holiday break, dealers said.
They expected the first week of April to remain quiet as many players were likely to extend their holiday.
"The Belgian market will slow down in the first quarter of April as investors are away on holidays," said one trader.
The Bel-20 index closed up 1.03 percent at 2,146.37, with three billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
Dealers noted that volatility was high near the end of the session.

"Investors will spend their holidays digesting the economic situation in the U.S....When they realise the Fed will push up interest rates soon, they'll start panicking and take profits," said one trader.
Electronics group Barco was the biggest gainer with a 5.87 percent jump to 5,950 francs in the wake of a 31-percent rise in 1996 current profit.
"6,000 francs (per share) is the top for Barco. There will be a lot of resistance above that level," said another trader.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert was another notable gainer with a 5.05 percent leap to 22,350 francs. One trader put the rise down to short-covering by one London-based player.
Cement maker CBR recovered from recent profit-taking to close up 2.84 percent at 3,440 francs.
Bourse newcomer hi-tech firm Systemat NV closed up 3.5 percent at 1,400 francs on its second day of trading.
